name: T-Bar Row
summary: A bent-over compound row performed straddling a barbell or dedicated apparatus to build back thickness and strength.

setup: Anchor one end of a barbell into a landmine sleeve or a corner, and load weight plates onto the working end.
Straddle the barbell facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and slightly bend your knees until your torso is angled at approximately 45 degrees relative to the floor.
Slip a V-handle attachment under the barbell shaft just beneath the weight collar and grasp it with both hands in a neutral grip.
steps: Brace your core, maintain a neutral spine, and lift the plates slightly off the floor to establish the starting position.
Row the barbell upward toward your lower chest or upper abdomen by driving your elbows backward and retracting your shoulder blades.
Squeeze your upper and middle back firmly at the peak of the movement without rocking your torso.
Lower the weight smoothly under control until your arms are fully extended.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight, and exhale forcefully as you pull the bar toward your torso.
cues: Drive your elbows toward the ceiling
Keep your chest proud and your spine locked
Pull with your back, not your hips

common_faults.fault: Using excessive hip thrust to heave the weight upward
common_faults.correction: Keep your torso stationary at 45 degrees and focus on moving the weight solely with your arms and back.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lower back under load
common_faults.correction: Set a strong hip hinge with an engaged core and chest elevated before initiating the pull.

precautions: Use smaller diameter plates (such as 25 lb or 10 kg plates) to allow a greater range of motion without bumping your chest prematurely.
Stop the set if your lower back fatigues and starts flexing.
